title: Build the Recommender
outcome: By the end, I can implement deterministic filtering, scoring and ties for a complete catalogue case.
scenario: A fictional book chooser filters a request before comparing preference scores.
given: Request: animal subject, at most 90 pages. Score 2 for illustrated and 1 for comic. Tie chooses smaller ID.
A animal90 illustrated prose; B animal70 plain comic; C space60 illustrated comic; D animal80 illustrated comic.

steps.label: Filter
steps.detail: A,B,D meet subject and page requirements; C fails subject.

steps.label: Choose best
steps.detail: Return D with both preference matches recorded.

steps.label: Deterministic output
steps.detail: Reordering the input rows must not change D’s unique winning score.

explanation: Eligibility and ranking answer different questions. C has a high preference score but is not an animal book, so it must stay excluded. The implementation needs a no-match result and explicit tie policy even when this example has a unique winner. Save rejected reasons for an explanation, not just the final ID.

counterfactual.change: Change D’s pages to 91, leaving every other field unchanged.
counterfactual.prediction: D becomes ineligible, so A wins with score 2.
counterfactual.reason: The strict excess over the 90-page maximum changes filtering before ranking.

student_task: Explain why B does not win after D is excluded even though it has fewer pages.
teacher_answer: Page count is an eligibility limit, not a ranking preference here. A scores 2 and B scores 1.
project_evidence: Save the recommender code, contract and this full trace; test the same records in different input orders.
limits: Toy preference weights do not imply shorter or illustrated books are universally better for all learners.
review_note: New fictional case individually matched to this topic, with computations and policy traces checked. Use for supported practice; preserve the independent assessment.
